scope: Intersection POS×OSS — adversarial dispute on cascade, race conditions, leakage paths

attacks.scenario: Multi-order race — 3 POS staff mark 3 orders PREPARED simultaneously
attacks.vector: Three concurrent PUT /api/admin/order/{id}/status with status=8 (PREPARED) within the same 100ms window
attacks.expected_defect: Outbox dedupe collapses one event; chime fires only once; wall display shows 2/3 orders
attacks.actual_behavior: Idempotency key sha1(orderId|oldStatus|newStatus|correlationId) — each transition has DISTINCT order_id → 3 distinct outbox rows. Each broadcasts to channel; OSS handler fires _markNewReady(id) 3 times for 3 distinct IDs. _echoMarkedReady is a Set — collects all 3 IDs in same tick. _hydrateFromRows skips them all on next poll. No race defect.
attacks.evidence: PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox.php:26..32 (idempotency includes orderId AND correlation_id) + public/js/admin-oss.js:420..423 (Set per id)

attacks.scenario: Chime spam attack — repeated PREPARING→PREPARED→PREPARING transitions
attacks.vector: Admin reverts order from PREPARED to PREPARING and back 10 times within 30s
attacks.expected_defect: Each transition fires chime → 10 chimes within 30s, customers stop trusting audio cue
attacks.actual_behavior: Each PREPARED transition correctly fires chime once. This is by-design behavior — admin intentional revert SHOULD signal. Burst-revert is not a realistic attack vector; the 4-second visual flash timer (admin-oss.js:457..465) is also reset cleanly per call. No actual defect class.
attacks.verdict: INTENTIONAL behavior — operationally rare, no heal needed
attacks.note: If owner ever reports spam concern, debounce window via Lodash throttle on _markNewReady could be added (V1.0.2 backlog candidate).

attacks.scenario: Wake-lock zombie — Vue route navigation away from OSS page
attacks.vector: Operator navigates from /admin/order-status-screen to /admin/dashboard while wakeLockSentinel is active
attacks.expected_defect: Sentinel persists after unmount, drains battery on tablet/operator surface
attacks.actual_behavior: public/js/admin-oss.js:253..278 beforeUnmount hook explicitly calls _releaseWakeLock() AND removes visibilitychange listener BEFORE the sentinel reference is nulled. The native sentinel.release() is invoked in _releaseWakeLock line 353. Also a passive defense: sentinel.addEventListener('release', () => null) handles browser auto-release.

attacks.scenario: Cross-branch OSS leak — Branch A wall fetches Branch B orders
attacks.vector: Customer-wall iframe on Branch A network calls /api/frontend/oss-order?branch_id=2 (Branch B)
attacks.expected_defect: Returns Branch B orders — confidentiality breach across tenants
attacks.actual_behavior: Returns Branch B's preparation queue, BUT payload contains NO PII (only order_serial_no + queue_number + status). The serial_no is the same number printed on the receipt — Branch B's queue numbers being visible on a Branch A screen is a UX issue, not a confidentiality breach. AND rate-limit `oss-public` 60/min/IP throttles enumeration. RouteServiceProvider:135..143 explicitly logs the threat model.
attacks.verdict: BY-DESIGN — anti-enumeration sufficient; PII payload empty

attacks.scenario: Source-surface allowlist bypass — DELIVERY order somehow surfaces
attacks.vector: Craft an Order with order_type=DELIVERY but token='X' and try to read it via /api/frontend/oss-order
attacks.expected_defect: DELIVERY leaks onto customer wall (was a real Wave 3c defect)
attacks.actual_behavior: Wave 3c heal at OrderStatusScreenOrderService.php:59..62 + 196..199 added whereIn(order_type,[KIOSK,TAKEAWAY]) FAIL-CLOSED allowlist. Even with a non-null token, DELIVERY is excluded. Verified by tests/Feature/OSS/OssCustomerScreenFilterTest.php::test_delivery_order_with_token_is_excluded_from_oss_wall.

attacks.scenario: DINING_TABLE/POS order with token leaks to wall
attacks.vector: Stale-test pre-Wave-3c data: POS=15 or DINING_TABLE=20 order with a leftover token
attacks.expected_defect: Same allowlist bypass — V1 dine-in disabled but DB might still hold legacy rows
attacks.actual_behavior: Same whereIn allowlist excludes both. Sentinel tests cover both (test_pos_order_with_token_is_excluded line 170, test_dining_table_order_with_token_is_excluded line 192).

attacks.scenario: Branch enumeration via OSS public endpoint sweep
attacks.vector: Attacker scripts GET /api/frontend/oss-order?branch_id=1..1000 from many IPs
attacks.expected_defect: Confirms branch existence + measures throughput across the SaaS fleet
attacks.actual_behavior: Per-IP throttle 60/min/IP (RouteServiceProvider:145..152). Distributed-IP attack would need ~17 IPs per branch to enumerate 1000 branches in 1 min — possible but high-friction. V1.0.2 backlog mentions distinct-branch_id-per-IP logging.
attacks.verdict: PARTIAL — V1 acceptable for single-tenant Le Cayenne; SaaS hardening backlogged

attacks.scenario: Echo subscription on public wall (no authed branchId)
attacks.vector: Public TV mounted at /admin/order-status-screen — authBranchId() returns 0 — subscribeEcho() at admin-oss.js:407 returns early
attacks.expected_defect: Public wall never sees live broadcasts; relies on 2s polling fallback only
attacks.actual_behavior: By-design. Public wall has no Sanctum token → cannot pass channels.php branch.{branchId} auth → cannot subscribe. Polling fallback at 2s (intervalMsWhenDisconnected) is fast enough for SYNC-2 8s budget.

attacks.scenario: Token replay — public viewer steals token from wall display screenshot
attacks.vector: Customer-wall scraper photo captures token='abc123' for someone else's order, attempts to use it
attacks.actual_behavior: The token is a public order-retrieval handle (already printed on the customer receipt). It allows checking order status, NOT modifying or authenticating. No write authority. Equivalent attack vector = picking up receipt from trash.
attacks.verdict: BY-DESIGN — token is not a secret

attacks.scenario: Idempotency-key clash across self-cancel + admin-changeStatus path
attacks.vector: Customer self-cancels (OrderService.php:1718 path) while admin simultaneously changes status (line 1864 path)
attacks.expected_defect: Two distinct paths dispatch OrderStatusChanged for same order_id with same final_status — outbox collapses one
attacks.actual_behavior: Idempotency key includes correlation_id (PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox.php:31) — each HTTP request has distinct X-Correlation-ID. Even with same (orderId, old, new), distinct correlation → distinct outbox rows. Plus self-cancel path is protected by lockForUpdate (OrderService.php:1681) → only one wins.

verdict: ZERO adversarial defects produce P0 findings. RED-OSS-07 (branch enumeration) is the only sub-P1 with deferred V1.0.2 mitigation; explicitly accepted by RouteServiceProvider documentation. Intersection POS×OSS is converged at this audit depth.
